function.uniprot_function: Antagonizes canonical Wnt signaling by inhibiting LRP5/6 interaction with Wnt and by forming a ternary complex with the transmembrane protein KREMEN that promotes internalization of LRP5/6. DKK1 binds to LRP5/6 with high affinity, preventing the formation of signaling-competent Wnt-Frizzled-LRP5/6 complexes. In complex with KREMEN1 or KREMEN2, induces rapid endocytosis and removal of LRP5/6 from the plasma membrane, further inhibiting Wnt signaling. Also involved in bone formation, embryonic development, and regulation of cell differentiation.

pathways.pathway_role_summary: DKK1 is a key secreted antagonist of canonical Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. It functions through two mechanisms: (1) direct competition with Wnt ligands for LRP5/6 binding, blocking formation of Wnt-Frizzled-LRP5/6 signaling complexes, and (2) formation of ternary DKK1-Kremen-LRP5/6 complexes that trigger rapid endocytosis and removal of LRP5/6 from the plasma membrane. Importantly, DKK1 itself is a Wnt target gene (regulated by beta-catenin/TCF), creating a negative feedback loop. DKK1 also activates non-canonical signaling via CKAP4 receptor to stimulate PI3K-Akt pathway in cancer contexts. Critical for bone homeostasis, embryonic development, and dysregulated in multiple cancers.

metadata.data_quality_notes: Good quality data with structural information available for C-terminal domain in complex with LRP6. Domain annotations well-defined from InterPro and literature. Limited quantitative kinetic data: only low micromolar Kd reported for Kremen binding from SPR; no precise Kd values found for LRP5/6 binding despite being described as 'high affinity'. No crystal structure of full-length DKK1 available, only C-terminal domain. Signal peptide cleavage site well-established. Glycosylation sites predicted but not fully characterized experimentally. No information on DKK1 isoforms beyond canonical sequence. Extensive literature on functional role in Wnt inhibition and disease associations.
metadata.modeling_relevance_summary: DKK1 is a critical secreted Wnt antagonist essential for modeling canonical Wnt pathway regulation. Key for modeling: (1) Competitive inhibition of Wnt-LRP5/6 interaction with overlapping binding sites, (2) Ternary complex formation with Kremen-LRP5/6 leading to receptor endocytosis, (3) Negative feedback loop as DKK1 is itself a Wnt target gene (beta-catenin/TCF regulated), creating dynamic pathway oscillations, (4) Dual role as canonical Wnt inhibitor and non-canonical pathway activator via CKAP4, (5) Extracellular secreted protein enabling spatial regulation and paracrine signaling. Limited quantitative binding data constrains kinetic modeling; low micromolar affinity estimates available for Kremen but not LRP5/6. Structural data supports competitive binding model. Essential for bone homeostasis and cancer models.
